title: metric-courier-adaptive-ingress-and-prefix-normalization
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build a lightweight, tenant-aware "metric-courier" ingress layer that accepts mixed Prometheus scrape, Prometheus pushgateway, and OTLP metric envelopes, performs prefix normalization and tag canonicalization, applies per-tenant adaptive rate shaping, and emits a stable, low-cardinality schema to downstream aggregators.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Metric courier accepts OTLP and Prometheus remote_write simultaneously and normalizes to canonical metric names with a retention of original labels in a 'meta_' prefix. 2) Per-tenant ingress QPS throttling prevents downstream overload; tested with 1000 tenants and synthetic high-cardinality spikes. 3) Streaming histogram summarization produces 99th/95th quantiles within 3% of baseline offline aggregator. 4) No added 95th latency > 10ms for warmpath metric envelopes under nominal load.
design_decisions: - Use existing telemetry-gateway as the host process to reuse auth, tenant lookup, and metrics export pipelines rather than a separate binary to reduce ops complexity. - Normalize prefixes with a deterministic rule: model_* -> model, inference_* -> inference, route_* -> route; store original keys in meta_original_metric. - Perform tag canonicalization via a small configurable canonicalizer table per-tenant with a fallback fuzzy matcher for common variants. - Implement per-tenant leaky-bucket admission with token-bucket burst allowance and an adaptive backpressure signal to clients (OTLP keepalive/429 with Retry-After for push). - For histograms, use the streaming HDR-style summarizer (microbatch window = 30s, emit async sketches) to limit cardinality while preserving tail fidelity. - Persist a short-lived LRU cache for tenant canonical maps to avoid repeated external lookups.
tradeoffs: - Extending telemetry-gateway increases binary complexity and risk; tradeoff is faster rollout and shared auth plumbing. - Canonicalization table requires maintenance; fuzzy matching reduces misses but can cause false merges. - Streaming summarizers introduce eventual consistency for tail metrics vs exact per-request histograms. - Admission control may drop low-priority metrics under overload; we plan to tag and replay critical metrics through a high-priority lane.
implementation_notes: - New module: metric_courier (Go). - Input adapters: prom_remote_write decoder, OTLP gRPC receiver (using collector proto). - Output: normalized OTLP/Prometheus remote_write to downstream aggregator cluster with product-specific routing. - Telemetry: self-observe courier metrics: ingress_rate, dropped_by_rate_limit, canonicalization_hits, canonicalization_misses, sketch_emit_latency. - Config: tenant_rate_limits and canonicalizer_tables stored in config-store (Vault-backed JSON), with hot-reload support. - Feature flag: metric_courier.v1.enabled (FF toggle per-cluster and per-tenant).
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for prefix rules and canonicalizer matching. 2) Integration tests: prom_remote_write and OTLP clients sending mixed payloads; validate normalized output. 3) Load test harness in staging: simulate 10k QPS with synthetic cardinality bursts; assert downstream SLOs. 4) Chaos tests: simulate exporter connectivity loss and verify backpressure and dead-lettering. 5) End-to-end smoke with canary tenant and dashboard verification.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): enable metric_courier for internal telemetry and 3 low-traffic tenants, observe for 1 week. Phase 2 (Gradual): Expand to customers that consent to early telemetry handling, increase rate limits. Phase 3 (Default): Flip FF to default and deprecate legacy ingestion path after two weeks stable. Each phase gated by SLOs and can be rolled back via FF or by unbinding the module instance.
migration_strategy: - Legacy prom_remote_write and OTLP endpoints will remain; metric_courier registers a new endpoint and a lightweight proxy will forward a sampled fraction of traffic to courier for verification. - For tenants that rely on label shapes, use a dry-run mode where normalization is recorded but not applied; report diffs to an onboarding dashboard. - Provide tooling to remap alerts/dashboards using a name-map produced by courier.
observability_dashboard_refs: Grafana dashboard for courier: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/metric-courier/metric-courier-overview (panels: ingress QPS, canonicalization hitrate, dropped_by_rate_limit, sketch fidelity vs offline), LogQL queries and sample trace: https://logs.redwood.ai/app/kibana#/discover?_a=(query:(language:kuery,query:'service:telemetry-gateway AND component:metric_courier'))
security_considerations: - All incoming OTLP endpoints authenticated via mTLS and tenant tokens; telemetry-gateway already enforces this. - Canonicalizer tables are stored in config-store accessible only to telemetry-admin role. - Avoid storing PII in normalized labels; detect and redact common PII patterns (emails, credit-card-like sequences) and send as meta_redacted=true.
open_questions: 1) Should we support on-the-fly tenant policy overrides via the Console UI, or require API+config-store changes? 2) What is the recommended retention for 'meta_original_metric' to balance auditability vs storage? 3) Where to centralize fuzzy matching rules: global vs tenant-scoped?
